title: Engineering wheat straw cellulose through phosphorylation into a crosslinked, antibacterial and biodegradable superabsorbent polymer
content: The non-biodegradability and associated negative impacts on the environment and human beings generated by the synthetic poly(acrylic acid)-based superabsorbent polymer (SAP) have accelerated the demand for natural, biodegradable, and eco-friendly alternatives. Therefore, in this study, a biodegradable and sustainable SAP has been developed from the processing of wheat straws (WS) through the production of a high-viscosity suspension (HVS). The HVS was further processed into a crosslinked and antibacterial SAP utilizing calcium chloride (CaCl2) and zinc pyrithione (ZnP) via solvent exchange (SE) and freeze-drying (FD) processes. The free swelling capacity (FSC), centrifugation retention capacity (CRC), gel fraction (GF), salt sensitivity index (SSI), absorption under load (AUL), absorption rate, moisture, pH and whiteness index of the developed SAPs were systematically investigated. The FD (control) samples showed maximum FSC in all three fluids, such as water (39.33 ± 0.73 g g−1), simulated blood (SB) (34.16 ± 0.90 g g−1) and saline solution (35.05 ± 0.64 g g−1). However, ZnP–CaCl2 (FD) exhibited 28.77 ± 0.36 g g−1, 27.58 ± 0.51 g g−1 and 25.66 ± 0.86 g g−1 in water, saline solution and SB, respectively. The CRC and AUL of ZnP–CaCl2 (FD) were 22.06 ± 0.92 and 25.01 ± 0.90 g g−1, in saline solution and SB, respectively. The SSI, GF, and pH of ZnP–CaCl2 (FD) were 0.87 ± 0.31%, 96.9 ± 1.03%, and 6.78 ± 0.02, respectively. The ZnP–CaCl2 (FD) SAP also showed strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Escherichia coli (E. coli), with 27 ± 0.76 mm and 15.97 ± 0.61 mm zones of inhibition (ZOIs), respectively, with 52% biodegradation within 60 days. These results suggest that the SAP obtained from the valorization of WS can be an alternative to petroleum-based materials in the near future.
